after: ## The three types in plain terms
alt: Two overlapping circles: product design, a physical object such as a storage unit or lamp, and digital design, a solution on screen such as a website, app or game. The overlap is combined design, where a physical part and a digital part work together, such as a board game with a scoring app. The design cycle and criteria are the same for all three.
caption: Product, digital or combined: same criteria, different evidence, tools and tests.

after: ## Evidence at each stage of the design cycle
alt: For each criterion, product and digital evidence side by side. A: research into materials and body sizes versus devices and accessibility. B: specification with sizes and materials plus sketches and CAD versus platform and load time plus wireframes and site maps. C: cutting list and build photos versus file structure and version saves. D: load and durability tests versus usability and device tests.
caption: The stages are the same; what counts as evidence depends on the type.

alt: A scale from low to high fidelity. Product prototypes range from card, foam or scale models to full-size prototypes in real materials or 3D prints; digital prototypes range from paper prototypes and static wireframes to clickable mock-ups and working builds. A 1:5 card model of a 900 by 350 mm stand is 180 by 70 mm: it tests proportions but not strength.
caption: Choose the lowest fidelity that can still run the test you need.

alt: Dot plot of eight users’ times to find a timetable page, from 9 to 31 seconds, against a 20-second target. The mean is 17.0 seconds, but only 6 of 8 users (75%) were under 20 seconds, while the specification needed at least 90%, so the point is not met.
caption: Check the proportion the specification asks for, not just the mean.

alt: Line graph of shelf sag against load: 0.6 mm at 2 kg, 1.3 at 4 kg, 2.1 at 6 kg and 3.4 at 8 kg, with a 3 mm limit. Assuming a steady rise between 6 and 8 kg, the safe load is about 6 + 2 × (0.9 ÷ 1.3) ≈ 7.4 kg, so the 8 kg specification is not met.
caption: Read where the results cross the limit, then plan an improvement and a re-test.

alt: A plant-watering reminder for a primary classroom runs as two strands through stages A to D: a product strand for the sensor housing (fits a 120 mm pot, survives splashes, 3D printed, splash-tested) and a digital strand for the web page (shows a “water me” picture within a minute; 9 reminders from 10 dry readings is 90%). The strands meet where the housing must leave room for the cable.
caption: Plan, build and test both the physical and the digital part.

alt: Ergonomics, sustainability and adaptation compared for product and digital design: fitting a handle to hand sizes versus touch targets and readable text; recyclable materials versus small files that run on older devices; adapting a product for a new user versus a layout that adapts to screen size. Innovation can combine both, as in a digital reminder for an ordinary plant pot.
caption: Each related concept shows up differently in product and digital work.
